clue.text: Very big female singer with rock group — maker of current waves

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer of the 1960s
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A huge diva performs with a rock band, making waves.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a well-known British singer and TV presenter; a tor is a craggy hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic device that generates alternating current produces repeating waves in that current.

clue.text: Gaudy insect on outside of tree

indicators.note: the insect word sits round the outside of the tree word, enclosing it

parts.note: a fly is an insect
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A brightly coloured bug perches on the bark of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for showy, garish display that tries too hard to impress.

clue.text: Lacking joy and merriment, having little energy in fact

parts.note: merriment is fun
E is the physics abbreviation for energy, a little bit of the word
in fact means really, actually

explanation.surface: Someone sluggish and humourless, lacking any spark of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning gloomily, in the solemn manner of a burial: without any joy at all.

clue.text: A little drink and girl's beginning to get unwell

indicators.note: the beginning of the word girl's is its opening letter

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A girl has a small drink and soon starts to feel poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter-pint measure, so a small quantity of liquor.

clue.text: Charged as signified, the first character to be brought out

indicators.note: the letter is to be taken out of the longer word

parts.note: signified means indicated
A is the first character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A legal report: someone charged, as shown, with the main person brought out of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first character' is not the first letter of a clue word but the alphabet's first letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: To be formally accused of a crime in court is to be charged.

clue.text: Not completely prepared for study

indicators.note: the word is not given in full: its last letter is cut off

parts.note: prepared means ready

explanation.surface: A student who has not fully prepared for revision.
explanation.definitionFit: To study a subject at university is to read it, in the British academic sense.

clue.text: Bad harvest — it's not hard to be very hungry

indicators.note: a bad version of the word is a jumbled one, its letters rearranged
says the letter for hard is not part of the result, so it is removed from the pool

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: After a poor harvest, it is not difficult to go hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges HARVEST once the H for hard is removed ('not'), leaving ARVEST to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is, informally, to be famished; literally to suffer from lack of food.

clue.text: The blues tunes — millions I'd played

indicators.note: the tunes and other words are played, i.e. performed in a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A blues band plays tunes about lost millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling the blues is low spirits, much like the disappointment of shattered hopes.

clue.text: Now and then look at princess on horse

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: Occasionally glance at a princess riding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse a book casually, reading bits from time to time.

clue.text: Greek character is quietly retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A shy Greek man quietly backs away.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the Greek alphabet, the one coming after chi.

clue.text: Orator to provide series of letters for someone making a book?

parts.note: to spell a word is to give its letters in order
a binder joins the pages and cover of a book

explanation.surface: A speaker asked to spell things out for a bookmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a book' suggests a bookie taking bets; here it is the craftsman who binds books.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker so compelling that the audience is held as if enchanted.

clue.text: Girl awfully lonely, having lost love

indicators.note: awfully signals the word lonely being rearranged badly
says one letter is gone from the jumbled pool

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A girl who is dreadfully lonely after losing her love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges LONELY once the O for love is removed ('having lost'), leaving LNELY to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, the short form of Ellen or Helen.

clue.text: Had tot to be heard in four groups of parents?

indicators.note: says the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: had means ate and tot means sum, an addition

explanation.surface: A toddler is fed and heard, while four sets of parents look on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child but is a sum. A Scottish reel for eight dancers, i.e. four couples: hence 'groups of parents', pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish reel danced by eight people, so four couples, like four pairs of parents.

clue.text: Good science that is evident in a form of cooking

parts.note: astronomy is the science of the stars

explanation.surface: A claim that good science shows up in a style of cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of preparing and eating fine food, a style of cuisine.

clue.text: Maidens perhaps work out — too much exercise may produce this

definitions.text: too much exercise may produce this

parts.note: a maiden is an over in cricket with no runs scored, so maidens are an example of overs
to work out is to train in a gym

explanation.surface: Young women working out at the gym risk overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; a maiden over concedes no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive exercise brings on an injury from pushing the body beyond its limits.

clue.text: Best old friend embraces tiny boy in Christmas story

indicators.note: the friend word wraps round the boy's name, holding it inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Tiny Tim is the sick boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: An old friend hugs a little lad at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning most favourable, the ideal choice.

clue.text: Extraterrestrial beings? They could give man a stir

indicators.note: the words could give another word when their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aliens who might give a human quite a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'could give' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed inhabitants of the red planet are archetypal aliens; the question mark admits they may not exist.

clue.text: Dejection ends as first sign of smile breaks out

indicators.note: the first sign of the word smile is its opening letter, and it comes first
the words break apart and re-form in a new order

explanation.surface: Gloom lifts as a smile starts to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dejection is low spirits, melancholy or unhappiness.

clue.text: Ruin created by little son, mad fellow?

parts.note: S is the short form of son
the Mad Hatter is the character in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Destruction caused by a small boy, or perhaps a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck completely, smashing something into pieces.

clue.text: Artist wants Guinness maybe when eating fish

indicators.note: the beer word takes the fish inside it

parts.note: Guinness is a stout, a type of dark beer called porter
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A painter fancies a pint of Guinness with his fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist depicts or represents subjects, so is one who portrays.

clue.text: Procession is cut, notice having interrupted it

indicators.note: the notice breaks into the middle of the cutting word

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A march is cut short after a notice disrupts it.
explanation.definitionFit: A march-past or procession, a line of people moving in order.

clue.text: Food dish — dad swallows a stone

indicators.note: the dad word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: pa is dad
ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A father chokes on a stone in his dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian noodles such as spaghetti or penne make a familiar meal.

clue.text: Possible financial agreement ahead of a match

definitions.text: Possible financial agreement ahead of a match

parts.words: Possible financial agreement ahead of a match
parts.note: a match is a marriage here, not a sporting fixture; couples may sign a deal on money before the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a sports fixture with prize money, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for prenuptial agreement, a contract settling money before a couple weds.

clue.text: Time with hint of modernity, as seen in car being developed

indicators.note: being developed means still in the making, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A new car model being developed shows a modern touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical period of rebirth in European art and learning marked the start of the modern era.

clue.text: One not first to grab work, offering negative response

indicators.note: the shortened word grabs the other inside it
the first letter of the word one is dropped

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone who won't be first to seize a job says no.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal no, a casual refusal.

clue.text: Arrogance of one in charge of paper is upsetting

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting means turning upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the person in charge of a newspaper

explanation.surface: An editor's arrogance upsets the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs, pretentiousness or a superior manner.

clue.text: Retreating sailor, a deserter

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, from tarpaulin

explanation.surface: A sailor in retreat is a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abandons a cause, as rodents are said to leave a sinking ship.

clue.text: Female novelist conjuring up pure unheard maid

indicators.note: conjuring up is magicking something new from the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman writer imagines a pure maid who has never been heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The English author of Rebecca and Jamaica Inn was a celebrated woman novelist.
